title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Maya Rodriguez
body:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended standards for service architecture and engineering practices. It is intended as the canonical reference for API design, coding standards, infrastructure and Terraform patterns, model-serving requirements, observability expectations, performance targets, and how to author/record ADRs. Owners listed per section are responsible for keeping guidance current.

1) API Standards (owner: eng-developer-experience):
- Purpose: Ensure consistent, discoverable, and stable interfaces across hosted, dedicated, and private products.
- Base rules:
  - HTTP first: RESTful endpoints for resource management (JSON over HTTPS). Unary generation and streaming endpoints allowed where needed.
  - Versioning: Use path-versioning: /v1/..., /v2/... for breaking changes. Non-breaking additions must be backward-compatible.
  - Consistent verbs: GET (read), POST (create/run), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE (delete). Avoid RPC-style verbs in paths.
  - Idempotency: POST endpoints that may be retried require an Idempotency-Key header.
  - Pagination: cursor-based pagination with fields: items, next_cursor, page_size. Prefer limit & cursor over offset.
  - Errors: Use structured error envelope: {code, message, details}. HTTP status codes map to classes: 4xx client, 5xx server, 429 rate-limit. Define stable error codes (e.g., MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE, QUOTA_EXCEEDED).
  - Rate limits & quotas: expose rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset).
  - Security: Bearer tokens via Authorization header; support audit logging and token scoping for private deployments.
- Telemetry hooks: All endpoints must emit request-level metrics (latency, success/failure, model_id, route).

2) Coding Standards (owner: eng-platform):
- Languages & style: Follow language-specific guides: Go: effective-go + gofmt; Python: PEP8 + black + mypy; Typescript: eslint + prettier.
- Linters & static analysis: Enforce linters in CI (golangci-lint, flake8/mypy, eslint).
- Tests: Minimum 80% unit coverage for library code; service-level PRs require unit tests and integration tests for critical paths.
- Dependency policy: Depend on pinned versions. Use automated dependency updates (dependabot) with owner approval for major upgrades.
- Secrets: No secrets in repo. Use runtime secret stores (Vault/KMS).

3) Infrastructure Standards (owner: eng-infra):
- IaC: Terraform modules under a central registry. Module inputs/outputs must be documented in README. Avoid ad-hoc cloud resources outside TF.
- Environments: canonical envs: dev, staging, prod. Deployments must flow through CI/CD pipelines.
- Naming & tagging: Use standardized tags: team, service, env, cost-center. Resource names: r-{team}-{service}-{env}-{component}.
- Networking: VPC peering and Transit Gateway for on-prem/private customers. Private deployments must support customer-controlled VPC and BYO KMS.
- Capacity & autoscaling: Define SLO-driven autoscaling policies; burst pools for Dedicated customers.

4) Model-Serving Standards (owner: eng-serving-runtime):
- Packaging: Models must include a model manifest (model_id, version, architecture, tokenizer, quantization_profile, kv_cache_compatibility).
- Quantization profiles: Catalog required: fp16, int8, int4 (experimental). Each profile must have measured accuracy/regression thresholds recorded in the model-onboarding page.
- Runtime compatibility: Models must declare required runtime features (kv-cache, rotary embeddings, alibi support).
- Rollouts: Canary (5-10%) -> Ramp -> 50% -> 100% or A/B with explicit success metrics. Automated rollback if error budget exceeded or quality regressions detected.
- Model validation: Onboarding requires offline eval against golden prompt set and a perf benchmark (latency, memory, throughput).

5) Observability Standards (owner: eng-sre):
- Metrics: Emit Prometheus-compatible metrics (counter, gauge, histogram). Required metrics: request_count, tokens_generated, request_latency_ms (histogram), model_cache_hits, batch_size_distribution.
- Tracing: Use OpenTelemetry. Traces must include trace_id, span for model-inference, kernel-exec boundaries, and downstream calls.
- Logs: Structured JSON logs (timestamp, level, service, request_id, model_id, message). Sensitive fields must be redacted.
- Dashboards & alerts: Per-service dashboards with SLO panels and error-rate, latency, and capacity utilization. Alerting thresholds: page on p95 latency breach > target for 10m OR error rate > 1% for 5m.
- SLOs: Define service SLOs and SLAs per product. Example SLOs: API availability 99.95% monthly; inference tail latency (p95) 500ms for hosted text-generation endpoints (configurable by model/route).

6) Performance Standards & Benchmarks (owner: eng-serving-runtime):
- Latency classes: interactive (p50 < 150ms, p95 < 500ms), batch (throughput-oriented, p95 can be higher). Policies must be declared per route.
- Benchmark suite: Maintain a canonical benchmarking repo (benchmarking-and-perf-suite) with representative workloads. Benchmarks must run nightly and before release for runtime or kernel changes.
- Performance review: Any PR that touches scheduling/kernels must include perf regression tests and a summary of results. Regression tolerance: no >2% regression in median throughput unless justified and approved.
- Cost/perf tradeoffs: Document quantization/ batching guidance per model with expected cost and quality delta.

7) ADRs (owner: eng-architecture):
- Purpose: Record architectural decisions that have long-term impact.
- Format (required fields): Title; Status (proposed|accepted|superseded); Context; Decision; Consequences; Date; Owners.
- Storage: ADRs live in confluence under architecture-and-standards/decision-records and a git-backed ADRs repo for diffs.
- Example decisions to record:
  1. Use path-versioning (v1) for breaking API changes.
  2. Adopt OpenTelemetry as tracing standard.
  3. Default quantization profile for edge models: int8 (when accuracy within 0.5% of fp16).

Operational procedures & rollout checklist (summary):
1. Author design and open an ADR when change affects cross-team contracts.
2. Create implementation plan with owners and test/rollback plan.
3. Run canary with telemetry and guardrails.
4. Monitor SLOs for at least one full business cycle before full rollout.

References and related pages:
- model-onboarding, quantization-profiles, benchmarking-and-perf-suite, observability-standards runbooks.
- See related ADRs for prior decisions.

Ownership & upkeep:
- Each section owner must review quarterly and note updates in last_updated. Major changes require reviewer approvals and an ADR for cross-cutting changes.

Appendix: Quick reference table (text):
- SLO targets: API availability 99.95% | inference p95 latency hosted (default) 500ms | error budget 0.05% monthly.
- Required toolchain: Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, GitHub Actions, Vault/KMS.

If you find inconsistencies or missing guidance, open an issue in the architecture-and-standards team board and tag the relevant owners.
